dedupe_keys.name: roofpedia registry of green and solar roofs

description: Roofpedia is an open registry of rooftop usage that maps which building roofs carry solar panels or vegetation, produced by a pipeline that combines deep learning and geospatial techniques to detect roof typology from satellite imagery. It covers more than one million buildings in 17 cities according to the arXiv paper of December 2020, and it also defines the Roofpedia Index, which ranks cities by how much of their roofscape is used for green or solar roofs. It was produced by Abraham Noah Wu and Filip Biljecki at the Urban Analytics Lab of the National University of Singapore. The code, the labelled training polygons (1,812 polygons for 8 cities) and the city results are available in the GitHub repository, and the trained model weights are available for download from figshare (about 1.2 GB). Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: the results are model predictions, and the list of cities is fixed by the paper, so coverage outside those cities needs the pipeline to be re-run. It is useful for mapping existing green-blue roof infrastructure and rooftop solar as inputs to stormwater, heat and distributed energy assessments; a related record is the Basel green roofs case study.
